REGION
REGARDING
PROTECTION
OF WOMEN
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1.
Regency Region is the Regency Region of Bekasi.
2. Regent is the Regent of Bekasi.
3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bekasi Regency
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region.
6. Woman is a person of female sex starting from infant, adolescent, adult up to elderly, who has been recognized by law.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the fields of politics, economics, law, education, social, culture and other aspects of life.
10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
11. Household is husband, wife, child, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability.
13. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
14. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
16. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.
17. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person
18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes.
19. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty.
20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance.
22. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations.
23. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence.
24. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health disorders they suffer.
25. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
26. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
27. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/area where violence occurred to the area of origin or family.
28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection.
29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems.
30. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
31. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.

Third Part
Women's Empowerment

Article 12
Domestic Violence as referred to in Article 8 letter d is caused by:
a. acts that neglect women within the household scope by a person who is obligated to provide life, care or maintenance to such woman;
b. acts that result in economic dependence by means of restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of a person; and
c. acts committed by family members that result in pain, bruises, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

C.
health services;
d. social rehabilitation services;
e.
legal services and/or legal aid; and
f.
repatriation and social reintegration services.

Article 25
(1) Empowerment of women in the field of education as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter b is implemented by the Regional Apparatus responsible for Education in the form of organizing formal and non-formal education.
(2) Non-formal education as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to improve the capabilities of women.
(3) Non-formal education as referred to in paragraph (2) includes women's empowerment education, skills education and job training.
(4) The organization of formal and non-formal education as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with statutory provisions.

Article 15
The provision of services to victims is carried out in an integrated manner by UPTD PPA.
(2) UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) may receive and send case referrals from or to other service units in a networked manner.

Article 24
women's empowerment in the field of (1) The implementation of empowerment in health as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter a is carried out by the Regional Apparatus that oversees health affairs.
(2) The form of empowerment in the field of health as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of health services to undergo reproductive life and sexual life that is healthy, safe, and free from coercion and/or violence.
(3) Health services as referred to in paragraph (2) include:
a. Health services during the period before pregnancy, pregnancy, childbirth and after giving birth;
b. Pregnancy regulation, contraceptive services and sexual health;
c. Reproductive health services; and
d. Services and provision of adequate lactation rooms in every Regional government institution, public facilities and industry.
(4) Health services as referred to in paragraph (2) are implemented through promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative approaches.

Article 27
Empowerment of Women in the field of law as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter d is implemented by Regional Apparatus and other related institutions in the form of:
a. increasing awareness and knowledge in the field of law through communication, information and education services; and
b. facilitation of access and legal consultation services.
(2) Empowerment of women in the field of law as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

3.10.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, the regulation clearly provides economic support/empowerment measures. Pasal 26 states: "Penyelenggaraan Pemberdayaan Perempuan di bidang ekonomi ... dalam bentuk: a. pemberian keterampilan dan pelatihan kerja; b. fasilitasi pembentukan dan penguatan kelompok usaha ekonomi produktif; c. fasilitasi pengembangan jaringan pemasaran." These are explicit economic support services (training, support for business groups, marketing network facilitation). The retrieved English candidate [3.10-40] accurately reflects Pasal 26, and the judge’s reasoning matches the text. Therefore the golden label 'No' appears incorrect.

4.1.evaluator_rationale: The policy includes prevention measures that explicitly involve socialization of relevant laws/regulations and education on women’s rights for the community as part of integrated efforts to prevent violence against women.

Article 5
Women victims of violence have the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling both from individuals, groups or institutions both government and non-government.

CHAPTER VIII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 38
(1) The community may participate in the implementation of women's protection in the region.
(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, business entities and mass media.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of: (4)
a. providing information or reporting to the competent authority if they become aware of acts of violence against women;
b. taking preventive action against violence against women;
c. conducting skills training for women; and
d. establishing social community institutions that handle the guidance and empowerment of women.
Further provisions regarding community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER IV
PREVENTION, PROTECTION SERVICES, AND EMPOWERMENT First Part Prevention of Violence Against Women

PPA;
e. involving the community in the implementation of women's protection.
f. providing adequate budget for women's protection programs according to regional capacity; and
g. conducting guidance and protection of women in the Region.

Article 33
To coordinate and synchronize policies, programs and activities for the protection of women to eliminate all forms of discrimination and acts of violence against women in the Region, the Regent shall establish a task force, forum, working group or other institution.
(2) The membership of the task force, forum, working group or other institution as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of relevant Regional Apparatus, community leaders, religious leaders, and universities.
(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment of the task force, forum, working group or other institution as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by the Regent.

4.1.rationale: The original Indonesian text explicitly includes information/education (socialization and education) as part of primary prevention of violence against women. Pasal 13 ayat (3) includes: (b) "melakukan sosialisasi mengenai peraturan perundang-undangan yang berkaitan dengan perlindungan hak perempuan korban kekerasan" and (e) "memberikan edukasi mengenai hak-hak perempuan bagi masyarakat." Pasal 30 huruf f also requires the local government to "melakukan sosialisasi peraturan perundang-undangan yang berkaitan dengan perlindungan perempuan korban kekerasan dan diskriminasi." These match the retrieved English passages and the judge’s cited snippet. So the policy does address information & education on VAW; the golden label 'No' likely is wrong.
